identity.title: Patient taps out the palpitation rhythm: regular vs irregular; rapid regular vs 'skipped beats'

technique.how: Ask the patient to tap the rhythm of their palpitations on the table with a finger, then classify it: fast and perfectly regular, fast and chaotically irregular, or a normal rhythm with isolated 'skipped' or 'thumping' beats followed by a pause. Estimate the tapped rate if regular.
technique.prerequisites: Patient must recall a typical episode; works best soon after symptoms.

interpretation.positive_finding: A rapid, perfectly regular tap suggests SVT, flutter or VT; an irregularly irregular tap suggests AF; isolated pauses/thumps suggest premature beats.
interpretation.negative_finding: A slow-to-moderate regular tap with gradual onset suggests sinus tachycardia or awareness of normal heartbeat; it does not exclude paroxysmal arrhythmia.
interpretation.pitfalls: No diagnostic-accuracy study of the tapped rhythm was found; patients frequently misjudge regularity and rate, and the palpitations RCE found the clinical examination cannot exclude significant arrhythmia. Symptom-rhythm correlation on a monitor remains the reference.
interpretation.changes_what: Irregular rapid tap: obtain ECG/ambulatory monitor for AF; regular rapid tap: monitor for SVT/VT; skipped beats: 12-lead ECG, reassure if ectopy and structurally normal heart.

sources.citation: Thavendiranathan P, Bagai A, Khoo C, Dorian P, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with palpitations have a cardiac arrhythmia? JAMA. 2009;302(19):2135-2143.
Weber BE, Kapoor WN. Evaluation and outcomes of patients with palpitations. Am J Med. 1996;100(2):138-148.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a 'benign' tapped pattern to stop the work-up in patients with syncope, structural heart disease, or an abnormal ECG.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: A rapid regular or irregular pattern with syncope, chest pain or dyspnoea requires immediate ECG and monitoring.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Unvalidated; interpretation of the tapped rhythm is clinician-dependent and no reliability data were found.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy data located. The anchor RCE (Thavendiranathan 2009, PMID 19920238; not open access) abstract lists the only history items with significant LRs (none concern patient-reported regularity) and states 'No other features significantly alter the probability of clinically significant arrhythmia'. PubMed search 'palpitations irregular regular patient description atrial fibrillation diagnostic accuracy' returned nothing. Weber & Kapoor 1996 (structured-interview cohort, 190 patients) is cited as the principal primary cohort behind the RCE; its abstract contains no rhythm-description accuracy. Record left not_quantified; the manoeuvre is supported by pattern-recognition teaching only.
